title: The Beak Broker's Cut
story: Every sale at the floating Raftmarket must pass through the gullet of Pellicrux, a gigantic grey pelican in a merchant's hat who swallows a slice of every deal and calls it business. Mr 6 has brought twelve glass lanterns to sell so the lamp-makers' children can buy winter blankets before the frost. Pellicrux clacks his beak and waits.
question: Mr 6 sells all 12 lanterns at 7.5 gold crowns each. Pellicrux swallows 20% of the sale as his beak fee, and then the raft-ferry charges a flat toll of 6 gold crowns. How many gold crowns does Mr 6 carry home?
solution: The lanterns sell for 12 x 7.5 = 90 gold crowns.
Pellicrux swallows 20% of 90, which is 0.2 x 90 = 18 crowns, leaving 90 - 18 = 72.
Then the ferry toll takes 6 more: 72 - 6 = 66 gold crowns carried home.
praise: Taking the percent off the full sale was solid thinking — there was just one more bite out of the purse after the pelican's.
hint: Find the whole sale first, then take the pelican's 20% off that — and remember the ferry is still waiting with its hand out.
victory: Mr 6 paid the fee with a smile and whispered, "You swallowed one-fifth; I kept four-fifths and the blankets." Pellicrux checked his own sums, honked in horror, and flapped off to study fractions.
imagePrompt: A huge grey pelican in a tiny merchant's hat looming over a lamplit floating raft-market at dawn, while a small number-six knight calmly counts glowing glass lanterns and gold crowns on a barrel.
